findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil if the user never visited or has no record for the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or `find_or_create`, which also handles the unique-index race.

findings.title: State-changing action on a GET request
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as GET and changes the notification level as a side effect. Email link scanners, prefetchers and crawlers will trigger it, and it is exposed to CSRF-style requests. It needs a confirmation step or a POST.

findings.title: Missing topic and guardian handling; level cycles on each hit
findings.body: `TopicView.new` is built with `current_user` before the user is checked, and `ensure_logged_in` only covers logged-in users, so a logged-out visitor to the emailed link gets a login error rather than a redirect back after login. The toggle is also not idempotent: a second hit (a reload, or a scanner) drops the user from regular to muted. The unsubscribe also skips `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`, the reason id and the MessageBus publish are not set.

findings.title: Added `render :show` inside shared perform_show_response
findings.body: This helper is also used by `show`. An explicit `render :show` in `format.html` changes behaviour for `show` and applies to any caller, which could cause double-render conflicts. It is needed here only because the template name differs for `unsubscribe`.

findings.title: Route order, and a dropped constraint without explanation
findings.body: `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` is defined before `t/:topic_id/:post_number`, which is fine. However, the `post_number` constraint was removed from the summary routes without explanation, and the line moves are unrelated churn.

findings.title: Typo in property name, and an unescaped title rendered with triple-stash
findings.body: `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled, and the template uses it consistently. The template renders it with `{{{ }}}`, which is only safe because `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side. Any change to that would introduce XSS.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, which other callers don't pass
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` is also used by other emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url`, such as digest or other builders. The missing interpolation argument will raise or render a broken link. The spec was patched to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which hides this.
